title: Building @retry(times=3): loops, except and re-raise

kcs.statement: A retry wrapper loops over its attempts, returns func(*args, **kwargs) immediately on the first success, and catches only the designated exception types in its except clause.
On the final failed attempt the wrapper re-raises with a bare raise inside the except block, which propagates the original exception and traceback instead of falling through and returning None.
times counts total attempts, not extra retries; the factory should raise ValueError for times < 1 when it is called, because a zero-attempt loop never calls func and silently returns None.

problem_ideas: Implement @retry(times=3) and trace attempts against a function that fails twice then succeeds
Predict the call count and the exception seen when the function fails all 3 attempts
Fix a retry wrapper that swallows the final exception and returns None
Add exceptions=(ConnectionError,) and predict which errors propagate on the first attempt
Decide what @retry(times=0) should do and make it raise ValueError at decoration time
Add delay=0.5 between attempts and compute the worst-case added latency for times=4
